plan.title: 12-Week Bench Press Strength Program
plan.jordanWelcome: I'm Jordan, your coach for the next 12 weeks. You came in with a 275lb bench press target — I've built the entire program around getting you there. Week 1 is your calibration week — the weights are set conservatively so you can focus on form and give me honest effort ratings after each set. I'll use your RPE data from this week to tune what comes next specifically to you — the more honest you are, the better your plan gets.

days.title: Upper Power
days.sessionFocus: Heavy bench baseline — 5×5 at 170lbs.

exercises.name: Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Your 275lb target starts here — this baseline load lets me calibrate your Week 2 progression exactly.

exercises.name: Barbell Row
exercises.coachingNote: Strong lats create a stable bench platform — this balances all your horizontal pressing volume.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Upper chest development that transfers directly to your bench press lockout strength.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.coachingNote: Vertical pulling balances the session and builds the lat engagement you need for bench stability.

exercises.name: Close Grip Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Tricep strength is your bench press lockout — this movement has direct carryover to your 275lb goal.

exercises.name: Face Pulls
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt health is non-negotiable with heavy bench volume — this keeps your shoulders balanced and injury-free.

days.title: Lower Body
days.sessionFocus: Baseline lower — establish your squat and deadlift loads.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Lower body strength supports your entire pressing foundation — Week 1 is about finding your baseline.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Posterior chain strength keeps your bench setup rock solid — strong glutes and hamstrings mean stable pressing.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without the spinal load — this builds leg strength while keeping you fresh for upper body days.

exercises.name: Walking Lunges
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral leg strength addresses imbalances that could compromise your bench press stability.

exercises.name: Calf Raises
exercises.coachingNote: Calf development for balanced lower body aesthetics — this completes your leg training.

days.title: Upper Volume
days.sessionFocus: Volume upper — 5×8 bench at 145lbs.

exercises.name: Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Volume day at 85% of your heavy day weight — higher reps build the muscle that supports strength.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.coachingNote: Mid-back strength keeps your shoulder blades locked during heavy bench — this builds that stability.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.coachingNote: Anterior delt strength contributes directly to your bench press power off the chest.

exercises.name: Cable Fly
exercises.coachingNote: Chest isolation that builds the muscle mass your bench press needs — constant tension through the full range.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown
exercises.coachingNote: Lateral tricep head development for arm thickness — this isolation targets what compound movements miss.

exercises.name: Barbell Curls
exercises.coachingNote: Bicep peak development for balanced arm aesthetics — this builds the mass that complements your tricep work.

days.title: Lower Volume
days.sessionFocus: Volume lower — higher reps for leg muscle building.

exercises.name: Front Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Quad-dominant squat pattern that builds leg strength with less spinal loading than back squats.

exercises.name: Stiff Leg Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation under stretch — this builds the posterior chain flexibility and strength you need.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squats
exercises.coachingNote: Single leg strength that addresses imbalances — unilateral work you can't get from bilateral squats.

exercises.name: Leg Curls
exercises.coachingNote: Isolated hamstring curl targets the knee flexion function that Romanian deadlifts don't fully address.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.coachingNote: Core stability is essential for maintaining tight bench press setup — this builds the foundation everything else requires.

plan.title: Full Body Hypertrophy Foundation

Your goal is building size — I've programmed 3 days with the volume and frequency that actually drives hypertrophy, and Week 1 you set your own starting weights aiming for something that feels like RPE 7 on each exercise. Week 1 is your calibration week — pick loads that match your effort targets and record them after each set; that data is how I tune what comes next. I'll use your RPE data from this week to tune what comes next specifically to you — the more honest you are, the better your plan gets.

days.title: Full Body A
days.sessionFocus: Baseline upper focus — chest, back, shoulders at RPE 7.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Your foundation horizontal push — this movement builds the base strength and size for everything else we'll layer in.

exercises.name: Barbell Row (Overhand Wide)
exercises.coachingNote: Wide grip targets your upper traps and rear delts — balances the pressing volume and builds the width you're after.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.coachingNote: Dumbbells force each shoulder to work independently — better for balanced development than barbell pressing at your experience level.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown (Rope)
exercises.coachingNote: Rope attachment lets you split the handles at the bottom — maximizes the stretch on the lateral head for arm thickness.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Dumbbells allow for full supination through the range — better bicep activation than barbell curls for pure arm development.

days.title: Full Body B
days.sessionFocus: Baseline lower focus — squat, hinge, quads at RPE 7.

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: The king of lower body mass builders — hits quads, glutes, and core in one movement while teaching you to handle load.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary hinge pattern — teaches the hip movement while targeting hamstrings and glutes through their full range.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Machine stability lets you focus purely on leg drive — extra quad volume without the balance demands of free weights.

exercises.name: Calf Raise (Standing)
exercises.coachingNote: Standing position targets the gastrocnemius — the muscle that gives your calves their diamond shape and size.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.coachingNote: Isometric holds build the deep core stability that transfers to every other lift — foundation work before we add rotation.

days.title: Full Body C
days.sessionFocus: Baseline pull focus — lats, rear delts, legs at RPE 7.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Wide grip emphasizes lat width — the V-taper muscle that creates your upper body silhouette from behind.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Dumbbells allow deeper stretch than barbell — better range of motion means more chest activation through the full range.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Single leg work forces each leg to carry the full load — exposes and fixes strength imbalances before they become problems.

exercises.name: Cable Fly (Mid Cable)
exercises.coachingNote: Isolation movement targets the pec fibers that adduct the arm — pure chest work without tricep or shoulder interference.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Direct medial delt work — the muscle that gives your shoulders width and creates the V-taper from the front view.

days.title: Upper Power-Hypertrophy A
days.sessionFocus: Baseline upper — 140lb bench baseline plus accessory volume.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary strength compound — this 140lb baseline establishes your power phase before we layer hypertrophy work.

exercises.name: Barbell Row (Overhand Wide)
exercises.coachingNote: Heavy horizontal pull balances the bench volume — wide grip targets your upper back and rear delts for pressing stability.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Low-angle incline targets the upper chest that flat pressing misses — critical for complete pec development.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Wide grip emphasizes lat width — the vertical pull your horizontal rowing doesn't hit.

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Lateral delts create shoulder width — isolation work since overhead pressing is restricted.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown (Rope)
exercises.coachingNote: Rope allows full tricep extension — targets the lateral head for arm thickness.

days.title: Lower Power-Hypertrophy A
days.sessionFocus: Baseline lower — 170lb squat foundation plus posterior work.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary leg compound — this 170lb baseline establishes your squat power before we add volume work.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Hip hinge pattern develops your posterior chain — strength work that complements the squat pattern.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Machine loading allows high quad volume without spinal fatigue — pure hypertrophy after heavy squats.

exercises.name: Walking Dumbbell Lunge
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral work addresses imbalances and targets glutes through full range — essential single-leg strength.

exercises.name: Leg Curl (Lying)
exercises.coachingNote: Isolated hamstring flexion — targets the muscle function your RDLs don't fully address.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Standing position targets the gastrocnemius for calf size — high reps match the muscle's endurance fiber type.

days.title: Upper Power-Hypertrophy B
days.sessionFocus: Upper variation — different angles plus 205lb deadlift power.

exercises.name: Conventional Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Your heaviest compound — this 205lb baseline establishes your deadlift power foundation.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Dumbbell range of motion hits different chest angles than barbell — strength work with unilateral demand.

exercises.name: Cable Row (Close Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Close grip emphasizes mid-traps and rhomboids — targets the muscles that retract your shoulder blades.

exercises.name: Cable Fly (High to Low)
exercises.coachingNote: High-to-low angle targets lower chest fibers — isolation work for complete pec development.

exercises.name: Barbell Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Barbell allows heavier loading than dumbbells — builds overall bicep mass and strength.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.coachingNote: Posterior delt isolation balances all your pressing volume — essential for shoulder health.

days.title: Lower Power-Hypertrophy B
days.sessionFocus: Lower variation — front squat power plus unilateral focus.

exercises.name: Front Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Front loading emphasizes quads and core — different strength demands than back squat.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: Pure glute extension under load — builds the hip drive your squats and deadlifts need.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Rear-foot elevated position maximizes quad stretch — unilateral strength that transfers to bilateral lifts.

exercises.name: Stiff-Leg Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Straight legs emphasize hamstring stretch — targets the lengthened position for hypertrophy.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Isolated quad extension — targets the lengthened position your squats can't reach.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.coachingNote: Isometric core strength — builds the stability your heavy squats and deadlifts demand.
